subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- October 18, 2026
body:
AcreetionOS just welcomed its first‑ever first‑time contributors with a fresh welcome message in the acreetionos‑code‑acreetionos‑server repo, giving newcomers a friendly hand as they start their open‑source journey.  

Development: The server side got a nice quality boost today when the CI pipeline added ShellCheck linting for shell scripts, catching style and security issues before they ever reach production. This aligns with the project’s focus on privacy‑first code and means Darren Clift and Natalie Cole‑Clift Spiva’s infrastructure is now a bit tighter and easier to maintain. If you’re curious about the behind‑the‑scenes work, check the changelog at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html and the technical docs at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html.  

Community: Meanwhile, the wider Linux scene saw two notable updates: the GNOME Project released its long‑anticipated GNOME OS Preview, giving users a taste of the next desktop wave, and the 2026 Linux Foundation Technical Advisory Board election wrapped up with a refreshed set of maintainers. Both developments keep the ecosystem vibrant, and we’re watching for any crossover collaborations that could benefit AcreetionOS users.  

Tip of the day: If you’re new to contributing, start with the “Welcome New Contributors” guide on the wiki (https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html) – it walks you through setting up your dev environment, signing off on our code of conduct, and submitting your first pull request without getting lost in the details. Happy hacking!
